'''Kinumaki Shrine''' (きぬまきじんじゃ) is a shrine in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|Q696388|qid=Q696388}}, {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|Q130290|qid=Q130290}}. It is identified with Watatsumi Shrine, a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}). It is regarded as one of the five major shrines of Tajima.

=== Overview ===
An old shrine counted among the ten myojin taisha of Tajima Province. Its principal deity, Ame-no-Hoakari-no-Mikoto, is a deity of sunlight and heat. In ''Kojikiden'', "hoakari" is interpreted as "ripe ears turning red," and as with other deities linked to imperial lineage, is connected with rice, so the deity is worshipped as both sun and agricultural god. It is the same deity as enshrined at Moto-Ise Kono Shrine in Miyazu, ichinomiya of Tango Province, where the principal deity is named Amateru-kuni-teru-hiko-Hoakari-no-Mikoto.

=== History ===
"Kinumaki Shrine Origin" states:

Enshrined deities:
Upper seat: Taketase-no-Mikoto
Middle seat: Amateru-kuni-teru-hiko Ame-no-Hoakari Kushitama Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto
Lower seat: Tamakushi-hime-no-Mikoto

In ''Kokushi Monjo, Butsuma Shrine Genealogical Tradition'':
Tayui-gō, Watatsumi Shrine, enshrined on Mt. Kinumaki in Kinosaki District
Deities:
Upper seat: Wadatsumi-no-Kami (moved from Watatsumi shrine at Oda'i county)
Middle seat: Sumiyoshi deity (moved from Sumiyoshi deity at Kamikura-yama)
Lower seat: Ama-no-Atae, also called Ōama no Hiko-no-Mikoto
Ama-no-Atae-hime-no-Mikoto, also called Ōama no Hime-no-Mikoto
Another tradition says: Kushihikata-no-Mikoto / Tamakushi-hime-no-Mikoto

Kebi district chief Seto no Sukune invited Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, Watatsumi-no-Kami, and Funadama-no-Kami, enshrined them, and appointed shrine attendants, with Kebi Yoshimaro serving rites.

''Shoku Nihon Kōki'' (Jōwa 9, 842):
Five shrines in Tajima Province (Keta District Yama, Ikazuchi, To, Hajikami and Kinosaki District Watatsumi) were entered into official shrine status.

''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'' (Jōgan 10, 868):
Promotion of deities including Tajima's Watatsumi to Junior Fifth Rank Upper.

''Engishiki'' temporary rites, myojin festival section:
Lists Tajima's myojin shrines including Watatsumi Shrine.

=== About Tajima Province government-offering shrines ===
''Engishiki'' temporary rites, myojin festival section:
Lists Tajima myojin shrines including Watatsumi Shrine.

Waka by Emperor Go-Daigo:
"Look up, in the Oda'i forest traces remain, deep too the blessings of Watatsumi deity."

Waka of Kinumaki Daimyōjin, foremost of the five shrines:
"Cutting through the strait, the sword stayed in the chest, now made divine in Kebi shrine-land."
